title: King and queen against king: shrink the box
outcomes: Uses the queen a knight's jump away to shrink the lone king's room
Finds a mate in one without stalemating, and a quiet move that forces mate in two
Plays king and queen against king to checkmate

steps.text: A lone king can be checkmated with a king and a queen. Use the queen to shrink the box the king can move in, bring your own king closer, and give the final check next to an edge. The queen works best a **knight's jump** away from the king: it covers many squares and the king cannot capture her.

steps.caption: The queen on b4 is a knight's jump from the king on d5. Most of the king's room is gone.

steps.title: Same king, the queen moves away
steps.prompt: The queen goes from c4 to a8, far from the king. Predict first: does the king have more squares or fewer?

steps.text: Two things to check before each move. Is the queen safe, so the king cannot capture her? And, if your move is not mate, can Black still make a legal move? If Black has no legal move and is not in check, the game is a draw by stalemate, however much you are ahead.

steps.caption: Qd6 would leave Black without a move, and the king is not in check: stalemate.
Qg3 is stalemate too. A quiet queen move that covers the king's last squares is dangerous.
A quiet queen move can win by force. After Qf3 the black king has just one square.

line.say: The king has only one square, d8.
Qa8 is checkmate: the white king covers c7, d7 and e7.

steps.prompt: While you played it out: was there a moment when you were not sure whether your move would stalemate? How did you check?
